svg.text: 1. Gray ramp: R, G, B out against gray in
R solid, G dashed, B dotted; diagonal = unchanged; lines apart = a color cast there
2. Around the hue circle: hue turned, chroma scaled
solid, left scale: hue turned (+ = toward the next name to the right)
dashed, right scale: chroma out / in (above x1 = more saturated)
3. Color plane: where each color goes (dot = in, line end = out)
a line toward the middle = less saturated; outward = more; around = hue turned
4. ColorChecker patches: in, out, and the move in numbers
5. Spectral sensitivity of the rendered brightness (dotted: the eye)
how strongly each wavelength drives the result's brightness, around a middle gray
6. By wavelength: dominant wavelength shifted (nm), purity scaled
solid, left: nm the hue moved (+ = toward red); dashed, right: purity out / in
polajuice curves: the look's color path through a 33-point lattice, sRGB in and out; hue and chroma in CIELAB (D65).
By wavelength (CIE 1931 observer): an RGB pipeline holds three numbers of a spectrum, so these are what the look does to a camera's rendering of each wavelength - not a film's measured curves.
